why: Once the choices are made it is a plain longest strictly increasing subsequence, and each index simply offers up to two candidate values. Run patience-sort LIS where each index tries both values against the state from before that index.
hints: You never need to fix the whole chosen array first: only values that end up in the subsequence matter, and each index contributes at most one.
Use the classic tails array (smallest possible last value of an increasing subsequence of each length). At index i, both first[i] and second[i] are candidates to place.
For each index compute bisect_left positions for both values on the current tails, then apply both updates. O(n log n).
pitfalls: Compute both placements before applying either, or the two values at one index could chain into the same subsequence.
Strictly increasing means bisect_left, not bisect_right.
